newsitem.title: LEBANON: Lebanon monitors urge combatants to avoid civilians.
newsitem.headline: Lebanon monitors urge combatants to avoid civilians.

text.p: A five-nation group monitoring a ceasefire in Lebanon urged Israeli forces and Hizbollah guerrillas on Tuesday to avoid civilian areas in their tit-for-tat war.

The group comprising the United States, France, Syria, Israel and Lebanon discussed over two days an Israeli complaint over the killing of an Israeli soldier on Friday by reaffirming the ban on firing from or at civilian areas.

"The Monitoring Group by unanimity reaffirmed the obligation for all combatants to act strictly in accordance with the Understanding of April 26, 1996, which prohibits attacks from and on civilian populated areas," the group said in a statement.
"It urged once more all those responsible to avoid using methods of operation which directly or indirectly endanger the civilian population and to show restraint and caution," the group added.
Israel had complained that Hizbollah guerrillas fired into the outpost of Dabsheh inside south Lebanon's occupation zone from a civilian-inhabited area.
One Israeli soldier was killed and two others were wounded in the attack. Four guerrillas were killed in retaliatory fighting.
The monitoring group met at the headquarters of the United Nations Interim Force in Lebanon (UNIFIL) in the coastal village of Naqoura inside the security zone.

The April agreement bans Israel and Hizbollah from firing from or at civilian targets but reserves for pro-Iranian guerrillas the right to fight Israeli troops inside a 15 km (nine miles)-wide occupation zone.
The agreement was made following Israeli-Hizbollah fighting that killed some 200 Lebanese, most of them civilians, in the last major outbreak of violence in the region.
